title: Example tests must reuse the shared pre-migrated db_uri fixture
answers: tests/examples test is slow on Windows CI because it creates a new sqlite database
example test reruns database migrations every run
how do I point an example test at a tracking database without migrating a new file
reuse db_uri fixture in example tests
body:
Symptom: The example test suite is slow in CI, especially on Windows, because each example test sets up its own tracking database.
Root cause: tests/examples/test_examples.py:test_typesafe_judges_example originally pointed MLflow at a brand-new SQLite file under tmp_path, so every run re-applied all database migrations.
Fix pattern: Take the shared pre-migrated `db_uri` fixture as a test argument, call mlflow.set_tracking_uri(db_uri), restore the previous URI with request.addfinalizer, and drop the tmp_path argument.
Constraints: Applies to example tests that only need a tracking store. A test that must exercise migrations or an empty database is a different case and should not use this shortcut.
applies: Tests under tests/examples that call mlflow tracking APIs.
says: Example verification tests take too long to run during automated continuous integration builds.
Continuous integration jobs are extremely slow on Windows when executing sample walkthroughs.
Speed up sample test suites by avoiding repeated tracking database initialization on each test.
Sample integration checks stall because database setup migrations run repeatedly during builds.
search: Example tests under tests/examples that call tracking APIs must use the shared pre-migrated db_uri fixture rather than creating a new SQLite database in tmp_path. Creating a fresh SQLite file causes tests to rerun all database migrations, making CI runs slow, especially on Windows runners. Tests pass db_uri to mlflow.set_tracking_uri(db_uri) and restore the previous URI using request.addfinalizer, though tests that explicitly exercise migrations or require an empty store must not use this shortcut.
